questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to learn useful ancient Greek words
How British people often don't say what they mean
Why British people apologise less than Americans
The long history of English grammar rules
questions.why: Beth says what we say and what we mean are sometimes two very different things in English.

questions.q: According to Beth, why do people often exaggerate when they speak?
options: To add emphasis or to be funny
To tell lies
To sound more formal
Because they don't know the right word
questions.why: She says we often use exaggeration 'for emphasis or for humour'.

questions.q: When Derek Bousfield's daughters say they've had a 'mare' at work, what has usually happened?
options: Something truly terrible and upsetting
They lost their job after an argument
They had a very bad dream the night before
Something small, annoying and a bit funny
questions.why: Derek says it means they've had 'a mild and potentially slightly humorous occurrence at work'.

questions.q: What do Beth and Pippa say about the greeting 'Hi, y'alright?'
options: It is rude to say it to people you don't know
People expect a long, honest answer to it
It just means hello; nobody wants your news
Only young people in big cities use it
questions.why: Beth says 'we don't really want to hear the answer', and Pippa's friend just means 'Hello.'

questions.q: Which example of understatement does Pippa give?
options: Saying an awful meal was 'less than perfect'
Saying 'I could eat a horse' when hungry
Calling a bad day 'an absolute nightmare'
Saying 'No worries' to a friend who is late
questions.why: She imagines an awful meal and saying, 'It was less than perfect.'

questions.q: According to Derek, why is understatement popular in British culture?
options: Because most British people are very shy
Because it is taught in schools from an early age
Because taking yourself too seriously is a no-no
Because it makes conversations shorter
questions.why: He says taking yourself too seriously is 'a no-no in British culture'.

questions.q: Why does Michael Rosen say 'It's all good' when a stranger steps on his toe?
options: Because it didn't hurt at all
Because he wants the stranger to apologise again
Because he's happy about it
Because he's a bit annoyed but doesn't want an argument
questions.why: He says he's a bit miffed, but doesn't want a barney with a stranger, so he says it's all good.

questions.q: What advice does Beth give English learners?
options: Avoid using British phrases until you're sure
Don't be shy; talk, and carry on after mistakes
Only speak English with your teachers at first
Always ask people what they really mean
questions.why: Beth says don't be shy, get talking, and if you make a mistake say 'No worries!' and carry on.
